title: The buddy on Linux — four decisions

steps.headline: When should the app ask permission to add the small helper to your desktop?

options.label: The first time you switch the buddy on (recommended)
options.summary: You are asked at the moment it is relevant, and only if you actually want the buddy. Anyone who never turns the buddy on is never asked at all. Downside: the buddy does not appear the instant you flip the switch — there is a question in between.

options.label: During first-run setup, with everything else
options.summary: Gets it out of the way while you are already answering setup questions, so the buddy just works later. Downside: you are asked about a feature you have not seen yet and may never use, and it lengthens setup.

options.label: Never automatically — only a switch in Settings
options.summary: The app never interrupts you; you find it yourself under Settings when you go looking. Downside: almost nobody will find it, so on Linux the buddy stays invisible in practice.

steps.headline: If you say no — or you are on a Linux desktop this cannot work on — what should the buddy do?

options.label: Stay hidden, with one line in Settings saying why (recommended)
options.summary: Nothing broken appears on screen. This is what happens today, except that today there is no explanation anywhere — you just never see a buddy. Downside: the feature is invisible, so you have to read Settings to learn it exists.

options.label: Show it anyway, parked in a corner
options.summary: You can see the buddy and read its messages, but you cannot drag it and other windows cover it. Downside: it looks broken rather than unavailable, and 'why can't I move this' is a support question forever.

steps.headline: When you turn the buddy off, should the helper be removed from your desktop settings again?

options.label: Remove it (recommended)
options.summary: Nothing you did not ask for is left behind, and turning the feature off really does undo it. Downside: switching the buddy back on asks you again, or at least takes a moment to reinstall.

options.label: Leave it installed
options.summary: Turning the buddy back on is instant and silent. The helper does nothing at all unless the app is running. Downside: something stays in your desktop settings after you switched the feature off, which is exactly the kind of leftover that is hard to trace later.

steps.headline: When an app update ships an improved helper, should it update silently?

options.label: Update it silently (recommended)
options.summary: You already agreed to the helper once; being asked again on every app update is noise, and a stale helper would mean the buddy quietly misbehaves. Downside: a piece of your desktop settings changes without you being told.

options.label: Ask again whenever it changes
options.summary: Nothing about your desktop ever changes without you seeing it. Downside: a prompt after app updates you did not think were about the buddy, which is the kind of nag people learn to click through.
